title: JavaScript values at API boundaries
outcome: Distinguish missing, null, false, zero, and shared nested state when adapting API data.
useCase: Support forms with optional flags, numeric limits, and editable tag lists.
benefits: Fewer invisible defaulting and Cancel bugs.
drawbacks: Boundary validation and draft ownership require explicit decisions.
version: Modern JavaScript / TypeScript · Vue 3.5 where applicable · browser APIs
cue: Absence is a contract. Copy only what you own.

trace.title: API values
trace.detail:
## Understand the idea

A browser receives values, not intentions. A missing field can mean “leave unchanged.” null can mean “clear it.” false and zero can be valid choices.

Decide those meanings in the API contract before choosing a default operator.

Use ?? when the fallback should apply to null or undefined. Use || only when all falsey values should trigger the fallback.

Destructuring and spread copy one level. A new outer object may still share nested objects with the original.

That can make Cancel accidentally change the saved record.

Treat JSON as outside input. JSON.parse proves that text is valid JSON; it does not prove that the result has a ticket ID, an allowed status, or a sensible array shape.

Validate at the boundary, then pass a stable internal shape to components.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Trace load → validate → adapt → edit draft → submit → accept server result. Keep server data separate from unsaved edits.

Test an absent field, explicit null, false, zero, and an empty string. They are five distinct cases.

If a nested structure is complex, copy the fields the form actually edits rather than cloning an entire model graph. structuredClone supports many values but not functions or every host object; it is not a universal serialization protocol.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail:
Using value || default can silently change a valid zero. Copying only the outer object can leak draft changes.

Parsing valid JSON can still produce the wrong type.
